    • Marjorie W.
      College Park, MD
      0
      1

      Feb 18, 2026

      Charged a $400 common space cleaning fee for a 4x4 apartment. I moved out days prior to my other roommates who decided to leave a some items in the common space (several items in the fridge and cabinets) after I had already vacated the property and removed all of my belongings. As per the lease agreement you are not permitted back into the apartment after signing the paperwork and turning in your keys, yet I am being held liable for these charges that I had no way of preventing? Of my 4x4 apartment, my 3 roommates also were charged $100-$200+ each for their induvial rooms requiring additional cleaning and I was the only person who was not. I informed the staff of this as well as video footage that I had taken upon my move out to displaying the condition that I left the apartment in was far cleaner then what they showed me. Clearly an unfair and unavoidable circumstance that must be corrected.

      Utility bills are also extremely inaccurate, nobody was present in the apartment in the month of January and the utility bill was more expensive then prior months. For a lease beginning in August you will pay for a full month of rent $1200~ only to be allowed to move in the last week of the month ($1200~ for 7 days). Not to mention the tricks they pull to have you mistakenly sign a lease on their website trapping you in a contract.

      AVOID THIS PLACE, PLENTY OF BETTER OPTIONS IN COLLEGE PARK!!!!!!!!!!!!!

      Loved my experience so far! The common areas and hallways are often clean and the amenities (study lounge, game room, pool, patio) are very cute. I only wish the pool was open all year round! In comparison to living in the Varsity, the maintenance team is 1000x times more responsive and faster. In addition, the management team here is always friendly and willing to help (unlike the Varsity, yikes!)
      Great place to live overall and I am really glad I chose it despite the price being a little (a lot) overpriced. The monthly rent is insane for college students, but I hope that this decreases in future years with the increased amount of living options in College Park in 2022.

      I have lived here for my one year lease. Before this I lived at the varsity; in comparison, the view has smaller rooms but it has a deck with a pool, campfires, grills, with ready propane tanks which I love. I take my friends here all the time.

      Maintenance is lighting fast, the workers here are polite. When I lost my garage key, one of the boys at the desk replaced it for me for free, he said next time the charge is like $120 or something . There have been two times where I lost my ID and it was returned to me by the security.

      All the people in the building are polite.

      Cons
      -smallish rooms
      -more expensive than varsity

      Pros:
      -pool deck
      -Fast servicing
      -understanding management
      -study floor
      -lenient about fees
      -two gyms one in each building
      -daily cleaning, everything is CLEAN
      -furnished
      -free internet
      -free cable
      -FANTASTIC maintenance, once they even came to plunge the toilet.
      - people who live here are nice
      -management seems to know and like all the residents .
      -close to school
      -no mosquitoes in the area.
      -Dog park nearby (but there's fleas)
      -lake within walking distance
      -grocery store within walking distance
      -food places like shanghai Tokyo and sweetgreen are accessible from the elevators, u never have to leave the building.

      Living here is fun!!

      The pool on the deck.

      MD, MD
      0

      Aug 20, 2024

      If you enjoy the fire alarm breaking multiple times a year, going off in the middle of the night, maintenance illegally entering your apartment, and predatory charging and cleaning fees, then this is the place for you. Your lease is structured such that you have to pay for the entire month of August, but are only allowed to move in at the end of the month. As for move out, you need to be completely out at precisely noon or you will be fined as well. Why a pro-rata rate is not used for these scenarios is plainly predatory. Additionally, we were charged $60 to remove a kettle WHICH ALREADY WAS IN THE APARTMENT when we moved in, and a single bag and can which were left in the refrigerator. The building management puts in a minimum amount of effort into keeping the builds functional and intact. You WILL notice scuffs on nearly every wall in the hallways, dented elevator doors, wall damage throughout the apartments and mold in the bathrooms. We were a four-some paying $5200 a month for a ~1000 square foot apartment, which is on the low-end of the rent per person.

      My son lived in University View for 3 years, and graduated from UMD spring 2021. I paid last rent and last utility bill, and deleted my bank info in University View system. But another $390 was unauthorized charged after his exit. Be awarded this. Their management hides your financial information in the system somewhere.

      My bank helped stop this unauthorized access, meantime I asked what's the bill. University View gave me a "bill". I hope I can show here. For example, bathroom damage $22.50, twice charged, room cleaning $87.50, twice charged.... Everything was charged twice, very suspicious it was a really "bill". I asked details. Bathroom damage was turned into bathroom cleaning. Room cleaning was turned into room paint, but $87.50x2?? He lived there for 3 years and left no any stain on the wall. I should be thankful not charging other paint!

      The last 2 months, my son sublet his doom to someone through University View. The person paid $200 for this process. My son transferred the lease and key to this person, and cleaned room before he left. I didn't think 2 month stay of that person costed almost $400 cleaning.

      Last I heard people said don't set autopay in some third party websites. Now I knew what it meant.

    • T H.
      Fairburn, GA

      Apr 12, 2019

      Lived in 3 different places in college park, University View is the best. It is very quiet as majority of residents are STEM major / foreign chinese students who are very study oriented and respectful. Every time Ive had a maintenance problem, it was fixed within a couple days. Walk to class is nice as its through a little river and some nature, and the internet is good enough for gaming.

      Ive lived in terrapin row before and it was a total shit hole, very loud with terrible roommates (obnoxious alcoholics, drunk 7 days per week up til 5am) that were art history majors equivalent who got into this university not based on their grades, which terrapin row paired me with after I asked them for STEM students to live with. Ive also lived in frat row, which was okay, but I had to share a room and bathroom with many other people - so there wasnt much along the lines of privacy.

      Overall, University View has by far been my favorite out of the three if I had to pick, and make sure to try out the chinese place right next to it. The chinese international students have told me its the closest thing you'll get to real chinese food in college park.
